## Summary

Investigated V2-23 (remove the dead `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`claude-task` agent-dispatch path) and confirmed it live in the repo: `ai-dispatch.yml` accepted `claude-task` with no job behind it, and the actual key-consuming workflow (`claude.yml`, an `@claude`-comment GitHub Action) had every historical run conclude `skipped` per `gh run list` — it never fired a real job.

Key judgment call: `orchestra-model-resolver.ts`'s `case "anthropic"` also reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, but that's a separate, live, customer-facing bring-your-own-key LLM provider feature (used across `llm-client.ts`, `prompt-eval-service.ts`, `prompt-portability.ts`, and the settings API routes) — unrelated to the dead agent-dispatch mechanism. Left it untouched to avoid deleting real functionality; documented this explicitly since the task's own success-criteria grep would otherwise have demanded removing it.

Removed the dead `claude-task` trigger from `ai-dispatch.yml`, deleted the dead `claude.yml` workflow, reworded the stale comments, updated `AGENTS.md`, and added a regression test.

**Real blocker hit and documented, not routed around**: this session's `gh` token lacks the `workflow` OAuth scope GitHub requires to push `.github/workflows/*.yml` changes (verified by an actual rejected push). Split the work accordingly — pushed everything else to the branch, and kept the actual workflow-file diff + new test as a local-only commit (`879508fc`) in the task workspace, ready for a session/credential with `workflow` scope (or the Owner) to push directly.

Opened **PR #578** (WIP): https://github.com/FChecklist/compliance-tracker/pull/578 — fully documents the blocker and exactly what's pending.
